concerns.text: FR-006 requires 'top 20 most influential substructures', but Integrated Gradients and standard GNN SHAP yield per-atom/per-feature attributions, not substructures. The mapping from atom attributions to discrete 'substructures' is chemically nontrivial (which fragmentation? BRICS? conjugated-system detection?) and is left undefined. Without specifying the atom→substructure aggregation, the top-20 list is not well-defined and Constitution VII is unimplementable as stated.

Validation of interpretability by checking that 'top-ranked features correspond to extended conjugated systems or known fluorophore motifs' is a soft, confirmation-prone check with no failure criterion: any attribution on a fluorophore-containing molecule will highlight conjugated atoms because they dominate the graph. Specify a falsifiable comparison (e.g., attribution enrichment vs. random-atom baseline, or held-out motif masking) rather than qualitative plausibility.

Experimental FQY is strongly dependent on solvent, concentration, and measurement method; public FQY compilations (e.g., FluorDB) aggregate values measured under heterogeneous conditions. The spec treats FQY as a single scalar target with no requirement to record or condition on solvent/measurement metadata. This unmodeled heterogeneity can dominate the error budget and confound both SC-001 and the attribution analysis; at minimum the spec should require capturing solvent/conditions where available and discussing it as a noise floor.

The edge case is raised but no requirement defines the response (e.g., minimum test-set size, fallback to grouped split, or explicit reporting of underpowered comparison). With a 10% test split of ~500 molecules and scaffold disjointness, a small test set is plausible; the spec should state the handling so SC-001's baseline comparison remains interpretable.
